Max Bill, Junghans kitchen clock with timer, 1956

A kitchen wall clock designed by Max Bill, with Ernst Moeckl, while he directed the Ulm School: a pale blue ceramic body, a white dial with thin grotesque numerals, and a timer below.

Source
Victoria and Albert Museum, M.224-2007
Creator
Max Bill and Ernst Moeckl, designers; Junghans, maker
Made
Designed 1956; the V&A also gives 1960–1970 for this example
Style
Ulm School (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Calm, precise, domestic
Evidence
Inspected the V&A’s primary image 2007BP8871 of object M.224-2007 at 1067 × 1600 px, through the V&A IIIF service.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A says the clock “was designed by Max Bill whilst Director of the Hochschule für Gestaltung (HfG Ulm)”. It gives glazed earthenware, glass, chrome, painted metal, plastic, and a quartz mechanism, a design date of 1956 with Ernst Moeckl, and Junghans, Schramberg, as maker. V&A M.224-2007.

The record describes the body as “coloured a pale blue” outside and white inside, moulded in an inverted “V” shape. V&A.

Observed

  • The body is a glossy pale blue shape like a rounded drop, wide at the top.
  • The white dial carries thin, light grotesque numerals 1 to 12, fine minute ticks, and small “JUNGHANS” capitals with wide spacing.
  • The hands are plain black strips with pointed ends, around a small white disc.
  • A round white timer dial below has small numerals every five minutes and a pale cream pointed knob.

Why it belongs

The dial is the Ulm part: thin type, an exact scale, and no decoration. The color and the curved body belong more to general 1950s domestic design, so the clock is a bridge object and not a core example.

Borrow

Set a scale with thin numerals and fine, even ticks, and let the scale be the decoration.
